title: Working with Franz Jackson and Art Hodes; Lil Armstrong
summary: Franz Jackson's band works summer jobs, Stickney and the showboat; the interviewer asks about promoters.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: It's pretty good. Yeah, we played nothing but the 50s. Yeah, but the French, that's the only band, isn't it? Well, no, not the only band. That's about the only colored band. But Art Hodes, you know, is far as strong. Because Art didn't get any much more? Yeah, Art gets a lot. See, Art goes on these tours and things, he and France. See, France just leaves his band and goes on the 50s.
But Art doesn't get any much more?
Yeah, Art gets a lot. See, Art goes on these tours and things, he and France. See, France just leaves his band and goes to Art.
But right in Chicago gets not that much more?
Oh, well, I mean, we don't depend just right in Chicago. Most of ours work for subways. They're rich people, see.
It's nice paying everything. You want to stick me?

Yeah, well we had him play Stickney. He was out there steady. I forget to call it the Red something. Red Arrow. Yeah Red Arrow. Well Al Wynn was with him then. I played out there with Lil Armstrong a couple of times, but he had Al Wynn with him then. I played with him showboat later. When I joined him, I joined him and went in the showboat. Then we went out east and New England did some concerts and things like that. But we're doing pretty nice. Most of August, we work most of August. It's nice pay. I work a Sunday there at $60.
Barbara Reed used to help promote those dances. Do you remember Barbara and Bill Reed? They used to help promote dances at the Midnight Sun in Chicago.
Oh, I heard of them. Yeah, I heard of them. But personally, I don't know them.
Yeah. She was helping Bill Marshall. Yeah, yeah, yeah. She was helping her or something.
